notes:
Version history: project videos keep readable snapshots and diff-based versions, with named saves, per-file comparisons, undoable restore, snapshot recovery and external-change import. Conflicts offer an explicit choice of BaoCut content or the disk snapshot. The default keeps 10 unnamed versions plus saved checkpoints within a size cap; per-transaction Undo remains in the editor and change receipts.
Document history: each document tab keeps up to 10 versions, shows changed blocks and restores an earlier version as a new version. Sealed versions remain readable after the rolling revision history expires.
Project Git: project settings show repository status, Commit to git and opt-in auto-commit for BaoCut-owned snapshot and media files while preserving unrelated staged work. Git initialization and local filter approval require desktop or CLI; Web can inspect and commit. Git operations stay local, and unsafe repository states pause commits.
Skills: a dedicated rail page supports ZIP, folder and GitHub import, package inspection, asset previews, editing, duplicate, export, restore and up to 20 personal skill versions. Brands can be global or project-specific BRAND.md files, created with an agent interview, a blank template or a brand skill. Message instructions override project, global and skill brand layers in that order.
External agents: desktop apps now include a matching CLI and offline tool catalog, using bundled Electron without system Node. Install the bundled BaoCut skill by link into .agents/skills and .claude/skills globally or under any folder; optional copies report when stale. Windows uses junctions. Skills shows the CLI, MCP and install status; Web is read-only for installation. The old skill path command and per-host install folders are replaced.
Elements: add overlay templates, editable brand-kit layouts and logos, recolorable sticker packs, animated Lottie packs, APNG images and community pet stickers. Online sticker assets are cached locally; official pet sheets are excluded. Asset insertion and its follow-up edit share one undo step.
Code compositions: Canvas scenes can bake through recorded drawing instructions, with sampled frame checks and browser-pixel fallback. WebGL scenes and local 3D assets are supported. Background bake jobs report their renderer, retry unpinned revision conflicts and stop when replaced; export rejects stale prerenders unless explicitly allowed. CJK punctuation measurement more closely matches Chromium.
Preview: full-frame bottom code compositions stay live during play, scrub and pause, with baked output used for export and failure fallback. Sandboxed module scripts load correctly, and a loading panel covers first-frame loading or fallback preparation instead of leaving a black stage.
Timeline editing: insertRange opens space across selected tracks; replacing a code bundle can ripple later items when its length changes. Locks reject the transaction, music beds and chapters stay put, and broken transitions are reported. Read-only transcript lanes merge per track.
Explainer videos: the refreshed template and craft choose the form and visual subject per topic, default to a short cut under three minutes and deliver the video, cover and publish copy for every version. Reusable narration, alignment, scene, assembly, caption, gap, footage and preview scripts support bilingual sound bites, picture-in-picture, transitions, pause tightening and safer replacement without overlaps. Guidance checks geometry against facts and uses measured narration timing.
Captions: agents can set placement and style. Cue splitting, burned-in wrapping and SRT/VTT/ASS export prefer Chinese word boundaries; unknown or oversized words may still split. Custom caption scenes gain active-word clocks, animated unit font reflow, previous-word and line-box geometry, per-line quotas, lone-tail joining and shape gradients, subject to their declared capabilities.
Transcription: repair outlier provider word times without collapsing the rest of a chunk. Qwen synchronous ASR uses the correct Chat Completions or DashScope endpoint, with bounded chunks, language and context hints, usage and native word timing when complete. Official Alibaba custom endpoints are detected; asynchronous filetrans models remain unsupported.
Home and projects: register an existing folder in place, search the project picker and open agent-created videos once their timeline has content. Unbound in-app sessions can create videos in a named folder or project after a dedicated confirmation. Link and open-media downloads can save to a chosen folder without importing a video asset.
Image generation: paste or drop PNG, JPEG and WebP reference images across the desktop prompt and reference row. Edit models ask for a concrete requested change. Web cannot accept these local-path image references.
Tasks and storage: show 20 recent finished tasks, reveal 50 older entries per click and clear visible history with Undo. Pending decisions stay available. Clients remove evicted ledger records, applicable failed or cancelled results receive extra retention, and unused artifacts from pruned tasks are released while Space-backed results and managed video media are kept.
Input and language fixes: multiline native IME composition no longer appends duplicate preedit text; missing document toolbar icons have fallbacks; preview and export diagnostics follow the interface language. CLI help handles growing command groups, avoids duplicate project flags and accepts bare edit-operation names in spec. Guides and open-media metadata are clearer for terminal agents.
Dependencies: update the Claude Agent SDK, align Tiptap and patch KaTeX, downloader and PPTX dependencies. Source builds refuse to overwrite output while an app from that output is running.
macOS packages are signed and notarized. Windows CPU, CUDA and Vulkan packages are unsigned, require an AVX2-capable CPU and the Microsoft Visual C++ v14 x64 Redistributable. Automated release checks do not cover UI/export workflows, live model or GPU inference, physical IME candidate windows or paid agent calls.
